activity_summary: At dinner the loaf was a penny and short by a finger. You paid threepence for the meal and sixpence for the week's firing and washing, once. The Sunday letter stayed folded for Thursday's carrier. Mistress Ansell said she would count the spoons after dinner. Master Verbeke sat at the end of the bench and did not speak.

entities.name: William Shakespeare
entities.context: Paid threepence and sixpence, and refused to open the Sunday letter again.

entities.name: Mistress Dorcas Ansell
entities.context: Laid the loaf against the notch, took the week's sixpence once, and said she would count the spoons after dinner.

entities.name: Alse Pinder
entities.context: Named the finger short, and said she would rather find a spoon than discuss one.

entities.name: Gillis Verbeke
entities.context: Sat at the end of the bench, nodded at the loaf, and did not speak.

facets.activity: Paid the meal and the week's sixpence

topics: the spoon count still to come

quotes.text: A penny, then, and short by a finger.

quotes.speaker: dorcas_ansell
quotes.text: Threepence for the meal, Master Shakespeare.
